ei.title: Advances in Technology Require New Concepts of Privacy
ei.subject: 11월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Advances in Technology Require New Concepts of Privacy

fullPassage: Technology changes how individuals and societies understand the concept of privacy. The fact that someone has a new ability to access information or watch the actions of another does not justify doing so. Rather, advances in technology require citizens and policy makers to consider how privacy protections should be expanded. For example, when cameras first became available for commercial and private use, nations and citizens struggled over whether new laws should be enacted to protect individuals from being photographed without their permission. The reconsideration of privacy brought about by this new technology re-affirmed a distinction between private and public spaces. It was determined by most cultures that people automatically gave consent to being seen — and thus recorded — once they voluntarily stepped into a public space. Although some people might be uncomfortable with the spread of surveillance cameras, citizens in most cultures have adjusted to the fact that giving up the right not to be observed in these circumstances causes less harm to the community than failing to have surveillance.

questions.passage: Technology changes how individuals and societies understand the concept of privacy. The fact that someone has a new ability to access information or watch the actions of another does not (A)[justify / encourage] doing so. Rather, advances in technology require citizens and policy makers to consider how privacy protections should be (B)[restricted / expanded]. For example, when cameras first became available for commercial and private use, nations and citizens struggled over whether new laws should be enacted to protect individuals from being photographed without their permission. The reconsideration of privacy brought about by this new technology re-affirmed a (C)[similarity / distinction] between private and public spaces. It was determined by most cultures that people automatically gave consent to being seen — and thus recorded — once they voluntarily stepped into a public space. Although some people might be uncomfortable with the spread of surveillance cameras, citizens in most cultures have adjusted to the fact that giving up the right not to be observed in these circumstances causes less harm to the community than failing to have surveillance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

① encourage(격려하다) — expanded — distinction: (A) 오답
② justify — expanded — distinction: 원문 일치 ←정답
③ justify — restricted(제한된) — distinction: (B) 오답
④ justify — expanded — similarity(유사성): (C) 오답

questions.passage: Technology changes how individuals and societies understand the concept of privacy. The fact that someone has a new ability to ①<u>access</u> information or watch the actions of another does not justify doing so. Rather, advances in technology require citizens and policy makers to consider how privacy protections should be ②<u>expanded</u>. For example, when cameras first became available for commercial and private use, nations and citizens struggled over whether new laws should be enacted to ③<u>expose</u> individuals from being photographed without their permission. The reconsideration of privacy brought about by this new technology re-affirmed a ④<u>distinction</u> between private and public spaces. It was determined by most cultures that people automatically gave consent to being seen — and thus recorded — once they voluntarily stepped into a public space. Although some people might be uncomfortable with the spread of surveillance cameras, citizens in most cultures have adjusted to the fact that giving up the right not to be observed in these circumstances causes less harm to the community than failing to have surveillance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① access: 정보에 '접근'하는 능력 — 적절
② expanded: 프라이버시 보호가 '확장'되어야 — 적절
③ expose(노출시키다) → protect(보호하다): 사진에서 개인을 '보호'해야 하는 맥락에서 expose는 반대 의미 ←정답
④ distinction: 사적/공적 공간의 '구별' — 적절

questions.passage: Technology changes how individuals and societies understand the concept of ①<u>privacy</u>. The fact that someone has a new ability to access information or watch the actions of another does not justify doing so. Rather, advances in technology require citizens and policy makers to consider how privacy protections should be expanded. For example, when cameras first became available for commercial and private use, nations and citizens struggled over whether new laws should be enacted to protect individuals from being photographed without their permission. The reconsideration of privacy brought about by this new technology re-affirmed a distinction between private and public spaces. It was determined by most cultures that people automatically gave consent to being seen — and thus recorded — once they voluntarily stepped into a public space. Although some people might be ②<u>satisfied</u> with the spread of surveillance cameras, citizens in most cultures have ③<u>adjusted</u> to the fact that giving up the right not to be observed in these circumstances causes less ④<u>harm</u> to the community than failing to have surveillance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

① privacy: 프라이버시의 '재고' — 적절

③ adjusted: 사실에 '적응'했다 — 적절
④ harm: 공동체에 '해'를 준다 — 적절

det.analysis:
① justify: 그렇게 하는 것을 '정당화'하지 않는다 — 적절

det.korean: giving up the right not to be observed (관찰받지 않을 권리를 포기하는 것)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ giving up the right not to be observed: 이 상황에서 관찰받지 않을 권리를 '포기'하는 것이 감시 실패보다 해가 적다 — 문맥 일치
❌ ① having access to new technology(기술 접근): 빈칸 뒤 'causes less harm'과 연결 부적합
❌ ② being photographed without consent(동의 없이 촬영): 앞 문맥 내용이지 빈칸 위치와 불일치
❌ ③ stepping into a private space(사적 공간 진입): 공적 공간이 맞는 맥락
det.tip: giving up the right = 권리를 포기하다. 공공 감시에 대한 시민의 적응

ch: giving up the right not to be observed
